core_classification.analysis: Natasha directly avows that she will continue to love Denisov, primarily presenting enduring affectionate regard as true. The future-oriented “always” also has a moderate promise-like or reassuring force, but it does not accept his proposal or undertake a marital relationship. Her emotional and hesitant delivery does not independently establish expressive/reflexive force.
core_classification.ambiguity: The future construction can be heard either as a prediction of lasting affection or as a limited commitment to continue caring for him; this supports moderate rather than maximal P.

utterance_status.description: Natasha directly addresses Denisov while refusing his marriage proposal and tells him that she will always love him nonetheless.

contextual_interpretation: The declaration softens a compassionate but definite rejection. Natasha has just told her mother that she is not in love with Denisov, yet finds him dear and pities him; accordingly, “love” here denotes continuing personal affection rather than reciprocal romantic love or acceptance of marriage. The utterance reassures Denisov and preserves their bond while explicitly withholding the relationship he requested.

evidence.quotation_or_description: «но не надо... это... а так я вас всегда буду любить» (“but it must not be… this… but I shall always love you all the same”)
evidence.supports: The contrast directly couples rejection of the proposal with an avowal of enduring affection, strongly supporting T and distinguishing the utterance from marital acceptance.

evidence.quotation_or_description: Before speaking to Denisov, Natasha says: «я не влюблена в него, должно быть не влюблена в него» (“I am not in love with him; I must not be in love with him”).
evidence.supports: Shows that the later love declaration concerns non-conjugal affection rather than reciprocal romantic love, without negating its truth-conditional force.

evidence.quotation_or_description: Natasha repeatedly says she feels sorry for Denisov and calls him dear or wonderful; after the refusal she kisses his head and later sobs on seeing his distress.
evidence.supports: Establishes the compassionate, consoling context. The emotion explains intensity but provides no positive evidence that the words themselves are a reflex-like discharge.

evidence.quotation_or_description: The highlighted form is affirmative and future-oriented: «я вас всегда буду любить».
evidence.supports: The future construction and «всегда» (“always”) support some promise-like enduring commitment in addition to the avowal.

ontology_assessment.diagnosis: T captures the avowal of enduring affection, while moderate P captures its limited reassurance or promise-like orientation. Emotional delivery remains contextual, and no important core force falls outside T/P/E.
